stories.headline: Cyclone Akwan begins landfall along India's east coast with strong winds and heavy rain
stories.title: Cyclone Akwan begins landfall along India's east coast with strong winds and heavy rain
stories.summary: Cyclone Akwan begins landfall along India's east coast with strong winds and heavy rain
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts early on Friday, says the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

“Latest satellite imagery indicates the land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts,” informed IMD on Friday (November 20, 2026).

“The severe cyclonic storm Akvan over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 21 kmph during the past six hours, weakened into a cyclonic storm and lay centred over the same region about 110 km southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 170 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha) and 250 km south-southwest of Puri (Odisha),” informed the IMD bulletin.

“It is likely to continue to move north-northwestward and cross the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by the forenoon of November 20, 2026, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 70-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph,” it further said.
Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch over seven to eight hours.
Meanwhile, coastal Odisha districts have started receiving heavy rain under the influence of the cyclone.

stories.headline: Supreme Court: Voters excluded from draft rolls can use ECI window to restore names
stories.title: Supreme Court: Voters excluded from draft rolls can use ECI window to restore names
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court Thursday asked voters left out of the draft electoral rolls to use the window opened by the Election Commission of India (ECI) to submit enumeration forms and restore their names, and that it would extend the deadline if needed.
It also observed that the question was how effectively the available window was used.

A three-judge bench headed by the Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant, with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, was hearing a plea by activists Anjali Bharadwaj and Amrita Johri on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process in Delhi.
Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for the petitioners, told the bench that the court had earlier asked the ECI to let deleted, who could not fill in forms, submit them.
He said that direction had not been implemented on the ground.
He also said the SC had described the use of Form 6 for voters on the Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate (ASDD) list as an error.
Such voters are not first-time voters, he said, so they should use the enumeration form, or Form 8.
The court had stressed that the ECI must reach every excluded voter by publishing ASDD lists in local languages at booth level and publicising them through WhatsApp and loudspeakers.
On November 6, the ECI wrote to Chief Electoral.
Officers of seven states, including Delhi, asking them to allow excluded voters to fill in enumeration forms.

stories.headline: Supreme Court grants interim custody of 4-year-old boy to German mother
stories.title: Supreme Court grants interim custody of 4-year-old boy to German mother
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday granted interim custody of the four-year-old boy of an unmarried couple to his German mother and allowed her to take him to Singapore for studies, rejecting the father’s claim that uprooting the child from his familiar environment in India will be greatly distressing to him.
A bench of Justices NK Singh and NV Anjaria said “the mother has a better prima facie claim of custody over the child” and “the balance of convenience lies in favour of the mother”.

“It is most likely that the child may suffer irreparable injury in the event the interim custody is not given to the mother, as the mother has a better/more concrete plan for his education and well-being in the interim, which is in the child’s best interests,” the bench added.
The SC clarified that the arrangement is interim till the guardianship petition filed by the father is decided by the Patiala House Court here.
The mother is a German citizen who ordinarily lives and works in a senior position with TikTok in Singapore while the father is a lawyer who runs a law firm in New Delhi.
Their relationship started in 2019, and the child was born in 2022 in New Delhi.
They never married.
During their years together, the family lived in Delhi, Goa and Singapore, but differences cropped up gradually and they approached reached courts, including the Supreme Court.
On August 11, 2026, the SC sought a report by the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS) to understand the child’s psychological and mental conditions.
The SC said, “From our observations during interactions with the parents and child, as well as from the NIMHANS Report, both parents are equally invested in the child’s well-being.
There is nothing to show that either parent cannot provide the warmth, compassion, care and guidance such a tender-aged child requires.”
It added, “However, the Report also mentions that the child is fluent in English and German, which indicates a close bond with the mother in her mother tongue/native language.
